newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria small banks must merge to survive - banker.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria small banks must merge to survive - banker.

text.p: Bulgaria's smaller private banks must merge or seek fresh investments to survive under a proposed currency board system, a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official said.

"Those banks should be urged to merge or to seek other ways to boost their capital and capital-to-risk assets ratio ahead of the planned introduction of a currency board system," the official, who declined to be named told Reuters.
Bulgaria's commercial banks are required to have a minimum capital of 2.2 billion levs for a full licence and 1.4 billion levs for a domestic one by March 31.
The central bank has said recently it planned to raise its minimum capital requirements for local banks in a bid to urge them to attract investors. No new levels have been specified so far.

An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission suggested last month that Bulgarian commercial banks should have four percent capital-to-risk assets ratio at the moment when a currency board system is introduced and a ratio of 12 percent two years later.
"IMF experts recommended a higher ratio than the internationally required one because Bulgarian banks operate in a more risky economic environment," the BNB official said.
Under international standards commercial banks are required to have a capital-to-risk assets ratio of eight percent.
Bulgaria has agreed to introduce a currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to boost confidence in the slumping lev and the crumbling financial system.
The currency board system is a form of a fixed exchange rate mechanism under which local currency in circulation must be exactly matched by the central bank foreign exchange reserves.
The BNB official said that the central bank would be not allowed to ease its requirements towards any bank under the currency board mechanism.
"Foreign experts proposed that smaller banks should close down voluntarily if they could not meet the requirements," the BNB official said.

Voluntary closure was considered as an alternative to seeking banks' insolvency through the courts by the BNB, which could ruin confidence in the banking sector and in the currency board system, the banker said.

The BNB put 14 state and private banks in receivership last year and filed insolvency suits against 13 of them citing their negative capital-to-risk assets ratios ranging between minus 2.4 percent and minus 56.6 percent.
IMF experts suggested that Bulgaria should focus its support on large banks which could have greater chances to survive under the currency board system, the BNB official said.

According to experts Bulgaria will need some $150 million to boost the capital of state banks that are crucial for the country's economy, said the official. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
